title: The Economics of AI Foundation Models: Openness, Competition, and Governance
abstract: arXiv:2510.15200v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Foundation model developers choose how open to make their models. Greater openness lowers downstream adaptation costs but can also make competing models easier to use. In a two-period model, an incumbent chooses its license fee and openness, a deployer adapts the model for users, and an entrant offers a competing model. Usage builds model-specific experience that lowers the deployer's future adaptation cost, creating a data flywheel that favors continued use of the incumbent. We identify conditions under which optimal openness falls and then rises as learning strengthens. The incumbent moves from full openness and a high fee to restricting openness for retention, then to a low fee that builds enough usage and experience to retain the deployer despite greater openness. A full-openness mandate can induce the incumbent to abandon this low-fee strategy. The higher fee can reduce first-period adaptation despite greater openness. An

translated_title: AI基础模型经济学：开放性、竞争与治理
translated_abstract: 基础模型开发者需要选择其模型的开放程度。更高的开放性降低了下游适配成本，但也可能使竞争模型更容易被使用。在一个两期模型中，在位者选择其许可费和开放程度，部署者为用户适配模型，而进入者提供竞争性模型。使用会积累模型特定的经验，从而降低部署者未来的适配成本，形成一个有利于持续使用在位者模型的数据飞轮。我们识别出了随着学习效应增强，最优开放程度先下降后上升的条件：在位者从完全开放和高许可费，转向为留住用户而限制开放性，继而转向低许可费策略——通过积累足够的使用量和经验来留住部署者，即便开放程度更高。强制完全开放的监管可能诱使在位者放弃这种低许可费策略；更高的许可费即使在开放程度更高的情况下，也可能减少第一期的适配。
tldr: 该论文构建两期博弈模型，揭示基础模型在位者的最优开放度随学习效应增强先降后升，并警示强制完全开放的监管可能适得其反，反而损害下游适配效率。
en_tdlr: Through a two-period model, this paper shows that an AI foundation model incumbent's optimal openness first falls then rises as learning effects strengthen, and warns that full-openness mandates can backfire by inducing higher fees and reducing downstream adaptation.
